scope: Local editorial subject curation for the policy and manufacturing installations from public pilot and development-v2 sources only.
interpretationRules: Keys are local semantic handles, not allocated registry IDs. These are final editorial choices for review, not an accepted or activated registry.
Parent edges propose topic containment subject to P2 review; they do not confer applicability, operational authorization, record lifecycle or source-authored taxonomy standing.
Warrant and alias evidence point to exact public source passage headings; nonliteral intermediate topics are warranted by actual descendant passages.
Related associations are authored once; inverse associations may be derived, never authored as duplicate inverse rows.
Co-membership in topics does not combine independent claims or broaden site, model, process or measurement-point scope.
Policy remains a deliberate flat nine-root forest because the development-v2 policy preamble explicitly requires a flat subject vocabulary.
The existing tolerances key is retained for assigned-key coverage but its label and definition are narrowed to pressure tolerances.
The equipment parent explicitly includes equipment retirement activity; equipment-retirement is contained as a topic, not treated as an object subtype.

classificationAbsence.treatment: Keep subjectKeys absent; do not infer assignments or substitute an empty set.

definition.text: Retention periods and policy history for customer support-ticket records.
includes: Ordinary and VIP ticket periods in the named regions
Supersession, conflict, rejection and archival clarification concerning ticket periods
excludes: Staff continuity and mentoring
Visitor-access-log periods
Deletion instructions with unknown record type

aliases.label: retention
aliases.context: Support-ticket records; resolve only where the surrounding statement identifies tickets.

definition.text: Programs intended to retain employees, locally represented by new-employee mentoring.
includes: The new-employee mentor check-in program and its cadence
excludes: Record retention or deletion periods
Support-ticket and visitor-log rules

aliases.label: retention
aliases.context: Staff continuity and new-employee mentoring; does not denote keeping records.

definition.text: Customer support work, its team, and records created in handling support tickets.
includes: Support-ticket policy context
Support-team proposals to use a privacy-analysis service
excludes: Visitor-access logs
Staff mentoring
Employee home-office purchasing

definition.text: Council decision-making about policy authorization, precedence and resolution of competing policies.
includes: Explicit supersession and conflict-resolution rules
Council proposals and unaccepted authorizations
Rejection of proposed policy extensions
excludes: Assuming a later date resolves conflicting rules
Treating a proposed authorization as approval

definition.text: Analysis of privacy matters through the external service contemplated for the support team.
includes: The proposed external privacy-analysis service and its contemplated activation
excludes: An inference that service use is authorized
Ticket-retention periods merely because both concern support

definition.text: Instructions or requirements to remove records, without assuming a particular record type or jurisdiction.
includes: The archived ten-day deletion instruction
Deletion as an explicit action distinct from archival preservation
excludes: Employee retention
Inferring applicability of the unlocated instruction to support tickets
Treating transcription acceptance as approval of the quoted rule

definition.text: Preservation, transcription and clarification of historical policy evidence.
includes: Preserving an archived deletion instruction
Clarifying a superseded ticket policy and its historical period
excludes: Reinstating historical rules as current policy
Inferring missing applicability from archival acceptance

definition.text: Mentor contact for new employees in the local staff-retention program.
includes: The mentor check-in activity
The program cadence of every 14 days
excludes: A 14-day record-retention rule
Support-ticket handling

definition.text: Minimum keeping periods and maximum deletion periods for visitor-access logs.
includes: The West visitor-log minimum and maximum obligations
Their unresolved incompatibility
excludes: Support-ticket periods
Assuming later acceptance supersedes the earlier obligation

related.rationale: Ticket-period rules concern support records; this is an association between orthogonal flat topics, not a parent edge.
The staff-retention program is implemented through new-employee mentor check-ins; both topics stay roots in the required flat vocabulary.
Competing ticket periods are addressed through council precedence and scoped supersession; governance is not inferred for unrelated rules.

definition.text: Production-process activities and their operating parameters in the local plant evidence.
includes: Packaging and sealing operations
Operating pressures and pressure tolerances, including historical or unlocated process evidence
excludes: Controller capability as an approved operating setpoint
Automatic applicability across plants or models

subjects.label: Packaging processes

definition.text: Packaging production activities, locally evidenced by Model R sealing operations.
includes: Packaging specifications and the sealing operation they describe
excludes: Gasket parts treated as operations merely because they are called seals
Equipment ownership without a packaging-process statement

subjects.parentRationale: Packaging-operation subject matter is contained within production-process subject matter; North and South packaging specifications provide direct descendant warrant.

subjects.label: Sealing operations

definition.text: The production operation of sealing, including its process specifications, sealing-head pressure and proposed changes.
includes: Plant-specific sealing specifications
Sealing-pressure trials and active-baseline statements
excludes: A gasket component called a seal
Controller input ceilings treated as process setpoints
An unlocated tolerance assumed to concern sealing

aliases.label: seal
aliases.context: Process engineering: the sealing operation, not a purchased gasket.

subjects.parentRationale: The local North and South packaging specifications expressly describe sealing operations; containment is of this local operation topic within packaging, not a universal claim about every form of sealing.

subjects.label: Operating pressure

definition.text: Pressure used or specified for production operation, including recorded values, proposed changes and allowed variation.
includes: Current and historical operating pressures
Pressure tolerances even when plant, model and measurement point are unknown
excludes: Controller input ceilings as operating instructions
Gasket materials and part identity
Transcription review treated as operational approval

subjects.parentRationale: Operating pressures and their variation are production-process parameters; archived process-note and historical line-operation passages warrant the topic even without present operating authority.

subjects.label: Pressure tolerances

definition.text: Allowed variation in operating pressure, locally represented by the archived plus-or-minus 5 kPa process note.
includes: Pressure deviations stated in pressure units
Unlocated and archival pressure-tolerance statements
excludes: Dimensional, material or other non-pressure tolerances
Treating the unlocated tolerance as an approved North Model R limit

subjects.parentRationale: This key is deliberately narrowed to pressure tolerances, which are variation limits on operating pressure; it does not denote tolerances generally.

definition.text: Plant-specific subject matter and attribution across the locally named production sites.
includes: North, South, East and West plant contexts
Plant-specific current, proposed, historical and inventory statements
excludes: Inferring a plant from an unspecified controller limit
Treating site co-membership as shared operating authority

subjects.label: North Plant

definition.text: Subject matter expressly concerning North Plant, including its equipment, processes, parts and history.
includes: North Model R specifications, trials and spare parts
Historical North Model Q operation and retirement
excludes: Applying South, East or West values to North
Assigning an unlocated tolerance to North

subjects.parentRationale: North-specific plant subject matter is contained within the broader plant-sites topic; the relation expresses topic containment, not a claim about equipment type.

subjects.label: South Plant

definition.text: Subject matter expressly concerning South Plant, including its equipment, processes and parts.
includes: South Model R sealing
South Model Q gasket and operating-pressure observations
excludes: North Model R spare applicability
Combining separate maintenance-book pages into a joint instruction

subjects.parentRationale: South-specific plant subject matter is contained within the plant-sites topic.

subjects.label: East Plant

definition.text: Subject matter expressly concerning East Plant and its local equipment or processes.
includes: East Model R sealing specification and local operating setting
excludes: Treating East settings as governing North or South

subjects.parentRationale: East-specific plant subject matter is contained within the plant-sites topic.

subjects.label: West Plant

definition.text: Subject matter expressly concerning West Plant and its equipment inventory.
includes: West ownership of a Model R controller and its input ceiling
excludes: Inferring an approved West sealing-process setpoint
Applying another plant’s operating setting to West

subjects.parentRationale: West-specific plant subject matter is contained within the plant-sites topic.

definition.text: Subject matter about production equipment, including model-specific operation, components and controllers, inventory and retirement activity.
includes: Model R and Model Q equipment context
Controller capabilities and ownership
Equipment retirement decisions and historical operating context
excludes: Treating a device ceiling as an approved process setting
Equating an accepted retirement record with a retired record lifecycle
Deriving plant applicability solely from a shared model

subjects.label: Model R equipment

definition.text: Subject matter expressly concerning Model R equipment, including its operating specifications, controllers and compatible parts.
includes: Model R plant-specific sealing and proposed trials
Model R controller ceilings and local gasket specifications
excludes: Model Q values or parts as Model R instructions
Assuming model co-membership removes site constraints

subjects.parentRationale: All subject matter within this model-specific topic concerns equipment, its operation or components, which the parent explicitly includes; this is reviewed topic containment rather than an object-instance taxonomy.

subjects.label: Model Q equipment

definition.text: Subject matter expressly concerning Model Q equipment, its operating history, parts and retirement.
includes: Retired North Model Q specifications and line retirement
South Model Q gasket and operating-pressure observations
excludes: Assuming all Model Q equipment is retired because the North line is retired
Model R operating or spare-part applicability

subjects.parentRationale: Model Q equipment operation, components and retirement form a narrower equipment subject, not a parent relation asserting that record objects are equipment types.

subjects.label: Equipment controllers

definition.text: Controller-device capabilities and inventory, especially pressure-setting input ceilings.
includes: The Model R 400 kPa device limit
West controller ownership and inventory
excludes: A site-approved sealing-process pressure
Inferring a site for the unlocated pilot controller artifact

subjects.parentRationale: Controller capability and inventory are contained in the parent’s explicitly defined equipment subject matter; this does not make device capability operational authority.

subjects.label: Equipment retirement

definition.text: Retirement activity and records concerning production equipment, including preserved pre-retirement operating history.
includes: The retirement of the North Model Q line
Historical operating evidence recorded with that retirement
excludes: Treating the accepted retirement decision itself as retired
Applying the retired line’s value to active Model R

subjects.parentRationale: The parent explicitly includes equipment retirement activity and lifecycle history, so retirement is a narrower activity topic rather than an object subtype.

definition.text: Physical gasket components described as seals, including material, identity and equipment-specific use.
includes: The North Model R silicone SG-8 spare gasket
The South Model Q nitrile NQ-3 gasket
Recorded silicone-seal material in the maintenance book
excludes: The sealing operation itself
Operating-pressure authorization
Assuming the South gasket is a North spare

aliases.label: seal
aliases.context: Purchasing or physical-part context: a gasket component, including an explicitly identified spare.

definition.text: Purchasing terminology and requirements for acquired parts.
includes: The purchasing sense of seal as gasket
The purchased-part standard specifying North Model R spare material and identity
excludes: Process engineering’s use of seal for an operation
Treating every gasket observation as a purchase or spare designation

definition.text: The explicit quality-review subject classification of a production specification.
includes: The extra quality-review classification on the East Model R sealing specification
excludes: Automatically classifying every reviewed record as quality review
Treating subject classification as approval or validation

definition.text: Equipment-maintenance subject matter documented through maintenance records and books.
includes: Historical Model Q specification retained for maintenance
Independent equipment, seal-material and pressure observations in the reviewed maintenance book
excludes: Combining independent maintenance pages into a joint operating instruction
Assuming a maintenance record approves current operation

definition.text: Preservation and transcription of historical process evidence whose original operating context may be incomplete.
includes: The archived pressure-tolerance process note and its reviewed transcription
excludes: Treating transcription accuracy as operating approval
Filling in missing plant, model or measurement point

related.rationale: The local sealing specifications state operating pressure at the sealing head. This topic association does not merge sealing with every pressure statement or turn controller ceilings into setpoints.
Purchasing identifies gasket materials and parts and uses seal for the physical part. Gasket observations need not themselves be purchases.
The purchased-part standard explicitly distinguishes the gasket and sealing-operation senses of seal; an association supports navigation while preserving distinct meanings and applicability.
